canonical_data: conversations, sessions, assistants, teams, and scheduled jobs in local databases owned by the desktop app and its backend, plus Markdown assistant and skill definitions
current_repo_note: The operational core is a first-party backend fetched as a binary from a second repository at packaging time, and the bundled engine is a third first-party repository; under ADR 020 the three are one product. The backend's package manifest declares a permissive licence that differs from its licence file. Reviewing this repository alone reviews the shell.
strengths: Team coordination is real machinery: a scheduler, mailbox, work coordinator, and crash recovery rather than prose
It works without any third-party tool because a first-party engine is bundled
A headless server and standalone web runtime are documented alongside the desktop build
weaknesses: The operational core is a binary fetched from a second repository at packaging time
The backend's package manifest declares a different licence from its licence file
Design documents and much of the changelog rationale are in one language only, and partner promotions precede the product description in the readme
why_it_matters: A desktop agent product where one runtime hosts a bundled engine and competing vendors' tools as interchangeable protocol workers, including in supervised teams.
